name: City Council Special Meeting of January 26, 2021
minutes_text:
APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL SPECIAL MEETING
  OF JANUARY 26, 2021

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE PARKING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
WATER AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:14 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Jessica Ancona, Mayor/Chair – present
  Maria Morales, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Alma D. Puente, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  m) Councilmember Martinez Muela
  s) Mayor Pro Tem Morales  4-0

4.  INVOCATION: Councilmember Martinez Muela

5.  FLAG SALUTE: Chief Reynoso

6.  SPECIAL MEETING PUBLIC COMMENT REGARDING AGENDIZED MATTERS ONLY:

  As provided under Government Code Section 54954.3, this time has been set aside for
  persons in the audience to provide comment or make inquiries on matters appearing on
  this Special Meeting agenda only. Although no person is required to provide their
  name and address as a condition to attending a meeting, persons who wish to address
  the body are asked to state their name and address. Each speaker will be limited to
  three (3) continuous minutes. Speakers may not lend any portion of their speaking time
  to other persons or borrow additional time from other persons. All comments or queries
  presented by a speaker shall be addressed to the body as a whole and not to any
   City Council Special Meeting Minutes of January 26, 2021

specific member thereof. No questions shall be posed to any member of the body except
through the presiding official of the meeting, members of the body are under no
obligation to respond to questions posed by speakers but may provide brief clarifying
responses to any comment made or questions posed. The body may not engage in any
sort of prolonged discussion or deliberation with any speaker or group of speakers on
matters that are not listed on this Special Meeting agenda.

Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police of the City of El Monte, or such member,
or members of the Police Department as the Chief of Police may designate, shall serve
as the Sergeant-at-Arms of the meeting. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders
and instructions given by the presiding official for the purpose of maintaining order and
decorum at the meeting. While members of the public are free to level criticism of
policies and the action(s) or proposed action(s) of the body or its members, members of
the public may not engage in behavior that is disruptive to the orderly conduct of the
proceedings, including, but not limited to, conduct that prevents other members of the
public from being heard when it is their opportunity to speak or which prevents members
of the audience from hearing or seeing the proceedings.
Members of the public may not threaten any person with physical harm or act in a
manner that may reasonably be interpreted as an imminent threat of physical harm. All
persons attending the meeting must adhere to policies barring harassment based upon a
person’s race, religious creed, color, national origin, ancestry, physical handicap,
medical condition, marital status, gender, sexual orientation or age.

Maggie Moe – Please appoint Irma Zamorano for the open City Council seat. Irma will
be a great team player and an advocate for the community. I support Irma and her
endeavors.

Danielle Zamora –My name is Danielle Zamora, I live in Arcadia and work at ActiveSGV.
I support Amy J. Wong for City Council because she is a dedicated community leader
who values equity, environmental justice, and public health. As an El Monte native, Amy
understands the struggles that need attention in her community and will prioritize
implementing an equitable Covid-19 recovery plan, building affordable housing, and
creating a more sustainable El Monte. As a first-generation Asian American, she will
bring greater diversity to the City Council. With 3 years of experience on the El Monte
City Planning Commission and over 6 years of nonprofit experience working on
environmental justice and public health in the City of El Monte, Amy is well prepared to
serve as a City Council member.

Andrew Yip – My name is Andrew Yip and I've worked in El Monte for six years and
have firsthand experience working with Amy. She's taught public health and nutrition to
high school youth, organized with them to push forth policies like the Complete Streets
Policy, led community bike rides, fought for more parks, and worked closely with some of
the businesses in El Monte for the Bike Friendly Business District. She believes strongly
in doing what is right and places the community first. We are at the height of a public
health crisis and El Monte routinely ranks second in the San Gabriel Valley in the
number of Covid infections and deaths. Amy has experience in public health and cares
deeply about the wellbeing of their community. She's helped me fundraise money to
purchase face masks and ear savers for distribution to front line and essential workers in
the area. She has a history of working with anyone that's willing to put the community's
interests first. It was the political landscape of racial injustice, public health crises, and a
deadlocked council that led her to make the decision to apply and commit to helping El

  2
   City Council Special Meeting Minutes of January 26, 2021

Monte brave through this storm. I ask that you please appoint Amy J. Wong to the El
Monte City Council. Thank you.

Sarah Hammond – I am a lifelong proud resident of El Monte and I wholeheartedly
support Amy Wong for council! She is exactly what this city needs to help combat hate
and bring in the peace! I just wanted to endorse my support.

Shahrzad Shishegar – Hello, I am very excited that Amy Wong is interested in running
for city council in El Monte. I've known Amy for over a year and I know her to be
hardworking, intelligent, and thoughtful in all that she undertook. She is organized and
responsible. She is an excellent listener and is prepared to research the issues for which
she advocates. In my opinion, the El Monte city council would greatly benefit from Amy's
presence on the council. Please consider her as a candidate for this position.

Bin Lee – My name is Bin Lee, I live and work in Pasadena, and spent my school years
in the El Monte/Temple City area. I still visit El Monte on a regular basis to visit friends
and eat at local restaurants. I support Amy J. Wong for City Council because we share
the same passion for environmental justice. I believe climate change is the biggest threat
to the San Gabriel Valley community and beyond. I've seen her dedication to advocating
for active and sustainable living up-close, and admire her compassion for the lives of
others. Both Amy and I understand that fighting climate change isn't just an isolated
issue. Passing environmentally-conscious city policies improves public health, attracts
innovation, boosts the workforce, opens up opportunities for all, and sparks the local
economy. In addition, as a Taiwanese-American, I believe Amy's Asian-American
experience will continue to contribute to El Monte's traditions of uplifting its citizens of
color. Lastly, her three years as Planning Commissioner shows her dedication to the city
she cares deeply for. Please appoint Amy J. Wong to the El Monte City Council. I
believe she will be an excellent addition to your fantastic team. Thank you for your time.

Wendy Chung – My name is Wendy, I am a second generation business owner at CNC
Electric Wholesales, which has been located locally in the South El Monte and El Monte
communities for more than 30 years. I support Amy J. Wong for City Council because I
know her to be a proud El Monte native with a strong vision and desire to see her
community thrive. Amy and I became friends while volunteering for an SGV-focused
nonprofit many years ago. I know that she is rooted and invested in El Monte. I believe
her experience growing up here, working here, and serving on the Planning Commission
equips her with the knowledge and insight to serve and represent the City. Please
appoint Amy J. Wong to the El Monte City Council. Thank you.

Jimmy Duong – My name is Jimmy Duong, I live in Monterey Park but I've grown up in El
Monte. I am currently working for Los Angeles County. I support Amy J. Wong for City
Council because she has the resume and the experience to know what it takes to plan
and improve for a better El Monte. Please appoint Amy J. Wong to the El Monte City
Council.

Ron Pang – My name is Ronald Pang I live in Alhambra and work retired from AT&T
after 21 years. I support Amy J. Wong for City Council because of her hard work and
enthusiasm she has demonstrated in servicing the need for the community of El Monte. I
feel her experience and knowledge will help to provide a better future for the city of El
Monte. Individuals with Amy's energy, compassion and talent are an incredible asset to

  3
   City Council Special Meeting Minutes of January 26, 2021

many organizations. I am positive she will make an excellent addition to the El Monte
City Council. Please appoint Amy J. Wong to the El Monte City Council.

Yvette Lopez-Ledesma – My name is Yvette Lopez-Ledesma; I am a resident of the
other valley, the San Fernando Valley and I work for the Wilderness Society, a national
conservation organization and I also serve as a Commissioner on the City of Los
Angeles Planning Commission. I am writing to you all to express my strong support for
Amy J. Wong for El Monte City Council. I have known Amy for over 6 years and can
attest to her strong leadership skills and love for the people of El Monte. Our work on
environmental issues brought us together and our vision of healthier communities keeps
us aligned. To call for a special election in a time where our public resources should be
appropriated to meet the needs of the current health crisis is unnecessary and frankly,
irresponsible. Amy is homegrown, committed, energetic and knowledgeable of public
processes. In her role as City of El Monte Planning Commissioner, she has developed a
strong base of knowledge, facilitation skills and a solid rapport with members of the
public and her fellow commissioners. Being raised in the community, she is most-familiar
with the opportunities and challenges that families and individuals work through day after
day. I am confident that Amy will bring a grounded perspective that is rooted in El Monte
and that will continue to work with the people’s best interests at the forefront. Thank you
for your time and consideration. I urge your appointment of Amy J. Wong for El Monte
City Council.

Pablo Tamashiro – My name is Pablo Tamashiro. I am a resident and the business
owner of Cyber Yogurt here in El Monte. I would like to express my utmost support for
Amy J. Wong for City Council. Amy has been a longtime advocate for environmental
sustainability and racial and gender equality. I believe that her experience and
knowledge in dealing with these issues would allow her to bring a great perspective to
discussions when the city is making decisions for our near and distant future. I have had
the pleasure to work alongside her in multiple projects over the last few years, and every
time she has been easy to work with. One of these projects is the Bike Friendly Business
District. The project’s main purpose was to encourage community residents to patronage
local business, while promoting a healthy lifestyle for the residents. Amy understood the
importance of balancing the interests of the community residents and those of local
business owners. She was always open for suggestions and willing to adapt when
needed, even when things got tough. When COVID-19 started, Amy and her team
adapted and continued to provide support to local businesses in the Bike Friendly
Business District. Although this project ended last year, due to our experience and her
influence I still continue to promote it and offer a discount to customers who bike to our
shop. I have also been lucky enough to get to work with Amy for a few other projects and
events including the El Monte Open Streets; which was not only successful, but also
incredibly fun. Her ability to work well with a team and communicate clearly and openly
made working with her a very pleasant experience. I truly believe that she would make a
great addition to the El Monte City Council. Thank you for your time.

Blair Miller – My name is Blair Miller. I live in Pasadena and I work for the Office of the
City Administrative Officer of the City of Los Angeles. I have served on Pasadena's
Planning Commission, Design Commission and Transportation Commission. For the
City of Los Angeles, I am tasked with converting City-owned property into affordable
housing and economic development opportunities. Through my career and my volunteer
service, I have had the opportunity to work with many City staff and elected officials, and
Amy Wong really stands out. I have known Amy for over 5 years through her work with

  4
   City Council Special Meeting Minutes of January 26, 2021

ActiveSGV and Day One. It is rare to find someone with Amy's combination of
commitment to her community, her leadership skills, her technical expertise and her
personal empathy. While I believe Amy would ably represent all the residents of El
Monte, as an Asian American, she would also bring important diversity to the Council. It
is vital for the residents of a city to see themselves reflected in their leadership. I hope
you agree that Amy Wong would be a hardworking, cooperative and progressive
member of the El Monte City Council, and that you select her to join you. Thank you for
your consideration of my comments.

Wen Lee – I am writing in support of appointing Amy J. Wong for El Monte City Council.
My name is Wen Lee and I live in Temple City. I have known Amy for many years
through her community work in El Monte and neighboring cities. I have watched Amy
organize group bike rides, community surveys, campaigns supporting local businesses,
educational events for children, and much more. It is clear to me (and everyone around
her) just how passionate she is about her hometown of El Monte and the people who live
in it. Amy is a hard worker and wears many hats. Sometimes I wonder how one person
can juggle so many things at once and still excel -- but Amy does. She not only gets the
work done, she goes above and beyond what's required, AND has a warm smile on her
face while she does it. You can tell she is having fun. One example comes to mind:
When she was appointed onto the El Monte Planning Commission, Amy dove right in.
She spent hours preparing for meetings, poring over huge binders of documents and
considering every detail before deciding how she would vote. Something that really
impressed me was when she started posting highlights from the Commission's activities
on Twitter, in an effort to inform the community about matters that will affect them and to
demystify what the Commission does. I have never known any Commissioner to do such
a thing and I think it is wonderful, brilliant, and so important. Most people are not
connected to their local city officials and don't know what they are doing. Amy sought to
change this. And that's what she is at heart: a change maker. On a personal note, Amy
is a good person through and through. She is kind, thoughtful, and honest. She's also
smart as a whip. I can't think of anyone better suited to serve on El Monte's City Council.
I hope you will appoint her. Many thanks.

John Lloyd – I am writing to offer my enthusiastic support for Amy J. Wong to be
appointed to the open seat on the El Monte City Council. I have known Amy for about 5
years through her work in several community nonprofits with which I am involved: Day
One and Active San Gabriel Valley. I have also followed closely her work on the El
Monte Planning Commission. In each of these roles, she has demonstrated outstanding
leadership abilities and a deep commitment to community service. The people of El
Monte would be well served by her presence on the Council. Allow me to provide two
recent examples of Amy’s positive contributions to her community. First, she is almost
single-handedly responsible for the outstanding “Women on Wheels” (WOW) program
she runs through Active SGV. This program has received national recognition for its
empowerment of women of all ages through its promotion of healthy, sustainable
transportation and community engagement. WOW is a model of Amy’s commitment to
grassroots outreach and engagement with underserved members of the community in
ways that are positive and transformative. My second example is Amy’s recent work on
the El Monte Planning Commission, where she has championed innovative solutions to
the city’s housing, economic, and public health needs. In my view, she not only has a
good grasp of these policy areas, but understands how they are interconnected. Our
community needs leaders like Amy to tackle the challenges we face in the 21st Century.
I’m not ashamed to say I’m a big fan of Amy’s. In my work as a Professor of Social and

  5
   City Council Special Meeting Minutes of January 26, 2021

Urban History at Cal Poly Pomona, as well as a longtime sustainable transportation
advocate in the area, I can say that it is rare to see a leader as young and talented as
Amy. I hope El Monte realizes how lucky it is to have her talents at hand and I sincerely
hope, Honorable Mayor and Council Members, that you will seat her on the Council
where her talents can be put to good use.

Johnny Lam – My name is Johnny Lam, I live in Chino Hills and partially in Alhambra as
I look after my mom. I support Amy J. Wong for City Council because when it comes to
community service I can’t think of anyone better representing the City of El Monte. I met
Amy through her work at Day One and with ActiveSGV (BikeSGV at the time) and her
willingness to step up and work towards improving her community is admirable. I’ve
been a resident of San Gabriel Valley off and on for over 30+ years and to see what she
and others have done to improve our communities with various events like “626 Golden
Streets” in the last few years has been amazing. Prior to these formidable years, I’ve
always felt our cities lack this sense of community. Given her prior experience in El
Monte Planning Commission, it should be an easy consideration for her to join El
Monte’s City Council. I have no doubt that she will strive to take care of her community
and make sure people are looked after. I am proud to call Amy my friend and look
forward seeing her excel in a leadership role in her own community. Please appoint Amy
J. Wong to the El Monte City Council. Thank you.

Dan Huynh – My name is Dan Huynh, I live in Pasadena, and work at Pasadena City
College. I am writing in strong support of Amy J. Wong for City Council. Over the last
four years, I have come to know Amy's character and leadership through her role at
ActiveSGV. As one of the leads for Women on Wheels (WoW), Amy has advocated for a
women-led space and collaborated with other women to develop valuable programming
that centers the experience of women of color. Since the program's launch in 2014, Amy
hasn't just been a program architect, she has also put in the legwork to sustain these
activities e.g. she often marshals bike rides to ensure participants' safety and comfort.
Her work with WoW highlights two character traits that I admire in Amy: team-
orientedness and a steady commitment to the work of creating equitable spaces. In
another example, during the 2018 summer heat wave, Amy accompanied me on a
canvassing activity for ActiveSGV. The two of us spent about an hour and half
canvassing local businesses on Garvey Avenue for the Bike-Friendly Business District
program. With everyone we met, Amy demonstrated patience and active listening. Even
when business owners waved us away, Amy was not discouraged. To her, their
skepticism only pointed to an opportunity for more authentic and durable community
engagement. I respect that she never puts the burden on any individual but endeavors to
understand where she or the larger system of governance could better serve the
community. As a council member, she would bring a humble, pragmatic, and systems-
based approach to problem-solving. I am convinced that Amy's appointment will add
value to the existing female leadership on the council. And what's more, her leadership
will finally give the Asian American community in El Monte a much-needed
representative. Please appoint Amy J. Wong to the El Monte City Council.

Phillip Tran – My name is Phillip Tran, I was a lifelong resident in the San Gabriel Valley
and just recently moved to Seattle in January to work on recycling and education
programs. I have lots of love and pride for the SGV and I support Amy J. Wong for City
Council because I have witnessed firsthand her undying commitment and love for her
hometown. I first met Amy in 2018 at a Bike SGV community event but had already
heard about her love and passion for sustainability work in the SGV through another

  6
   City Council Special Meeting Minutes of January 26, 2021

friend of mine. Her unwavering support and passion for a greener and more equitable
future was one of my first impressions of her. As I learned more about Bike SGV - now
named Active SGV, I also learned more about Amy and why she feels so passionate
about the work that she is in, which is why she is running. I continued seeking
opportunities to contribute to my community, so Amy told me about The Nature For All
Leadership Academy, a long-term training program that teaches organizing and
advocacy skills to encourage civic engagement. Not only did she help organize,
manage, and lead the program, but she was also leading the community to the brighter
future she envisioned for her community. Since that time she has continued pushing for
a greener and more equitable future. Her relentless passion and tenacity are the traits all
city council members should embody. Please appoint Amy J. Wong to the El Monte City
Council. Thank you.

Alexis Smith – My name is Alexis Smith and I am a primary care physician. I work in
a Medicaid health clinic in El Monte. I support Ms. Amy J. Wong for City Council
because she cares about the issues that matter the most to my patients. Every day I
am talking to patients diagnosed with COVID 19. Due to unaffordable housing and
crowding, this virus is affecting El Monte at higher rates than most other areas of
the San Gabriel Valley. Every day I also see patients suffering from food and
housing insecurity and chronic conditions caused by poor air quality. Many are also
struggling with employment issues and chronic disease related to previous limited
access to health care. I have gotten to know Ms. Amy J. Wong through friends who
are a part of nonprofit organizations engaging in improvement projects for the San
Gabriel Valley. Ms. Amy J. Wong has told me that she wants to focus on equitable
healthcare and COVID 19 recovery, affordable housing and ending homelessness,
and creating better air quality to reduce the development of chronic diseases. She is
a citizen of El Monte, is progressive, and does not receive funding from special
interest. When I hear her speak about her work, her passion for a better and more
just world is palpable. Ms. Amy J. Wong knows how to turn her visions about health
and environmental justice into reality. She has dedicated her post-university life and
work to helping others. She is educated about science and technology and has used
this knowledge to develop solutions to problems facing her community. Specifically,
she has engaged in many climate projects, worked for three years on the El Monte
Planning commission, and volunteered for several community nonprofits. She is well
versed in grant writing as well as working in groups, well organized, and knows how
to get projects done. In my experience with her she is also kind hearted and a terrific
active listener: she is great at meeting new people and forming alliances with them.
I believe the best kind of candidate for any position has passion and dedication
combined with experience and ability. This is Ms. Amy J. Wong. Please appoint Ms.
Amy J. Wong to the El Monte City Council. Thank you.

Kenny Uong – My name is Kenny Uong and I am a transit advocate and urban
planning student from Glendale, California. I support Amy J. Wong for City Council
because Amy has many years of experience working, volunteering, and advocating
for El Monte. I met Amy when I attended ActiveSGV’s open streets events. Amy is
dedicated to values of equity and justice, as well as to community-based public
health and environmental justice work in El Monte and the San Gabriel Valley. Some
of Amy’s top priorities for El Monte include protecting the most vulnerable during the
COVID-19 pandemic, supporting small businesses, building affordable housing, and
creating a more sustainable and livable city. It is very important now more than ever
to not only represent but also serve the community through the multiple crises

  7
   City Council Special Meeting Minutes of January 26, 2021

including the COVID-19 pandemic, climate crisis, and racial injustice. As a city
council member, Amy will help lead El Monte into a brighter future. Please consider
appointing Amy J. Wong to the El Monte City Council. Thank you.

Marissa Lopez – My name is Marissa Lopez and I grew up in El Monte and currently
work at Volunteers of America Los Angeles as a social worker. I support the
appointment of Amy J. Wong to the City Council because of her dedication to the
city of El Monte and her passion for justice and equity for the community. I had the
privilege of being mentored by Amy and current El Monte Union High School District
board member David Diaz when I was a student in the Day One organization at
Mountain View High School. Amy proved herself to be such a dedicated and
inspiring leader. It was under her leadership that I gained my first exposure to giving
back to my community through service and education. Amy supported and guided
me and my peers to be advocates and to use our voices to make real change in our
city, despite our age. Whether it was educating community members at health fairs,
advocating for bike lanes in El Monte at City Council meetings, or challenges to
reimagine our community with sustainable and healthy possibilities, Amy helped
open my eyes to what is possible when citizens work together for change. If you
select Amy J. Wong to the El Monte city council, I trust that she will make equitable
decisions and lead our community in the right direction because of her past actions
and because she has shown herself to be a person of her word. She deeply cares
about the people who live in El Monte as well as creating a community where
everyone has a chance to thrive. She first demonstrated this care through her
mentorship of a group of teenagers in Day One and has since taken her passion
and values to a greater scale. I strongly believe that Amy will be a wonderful
addition to the El Monte City Council and that she will join in the work to provide the
best for the citizens of our hometown. Please appoint Amy J. Wong to the El Monte
City Council.

Emily Ng – My name is Emily Ng. I am a resident of South Pasadena and working to
build capacity in local government to address environmental injustices. I am writing
in support of Amy J. Wong’s appointment to El Monte City Council. I met Amy in
2016 while she was working at environmental justice non-profit, Nature For All, and
leading a program empowering youth of color to advocate for local environmental
justice issues. As a youth participant, I was immediately inspired by Amy’s level of
dedication to her community. Amy has always acted with her community in mind,
and in the five years that I have known her, she has continued to be a prominent
and well-respected leader throughout the San Gabriel Valley for her active
transportation advocacy work. Amy’s background in community non-profit work
coupled with her experience in local city government, as Chair of the Planning
Commission, brings a multi-dimensional perspective to City Council. She is fully
attuned and dedicated to act on the needs of all residents in her diverse community.
Amy’s work and passion strongly centers equity, and she is committed to uplifting
voices of all community members, especially those traditionally left out. Her work at
ActiveSGV, through her position as Community Councilmember for Bold Vision and
as co-founder of Women on Wheels, has empowered youth of color and women by
giving them the tools and platform to engage in political conversations and activities
they are typically excluded from. Recognizing hurdles individuals may experience,
Amy has also worked to streamline the complaint submission process for
environmental justice communities to report poor air quality and polluters through
the South Coast AQMD Environmental Justice Inter-Agency Task Force. Amy

  8
   City Council Special Meeting Minutes of January 26, 2021

upholds values of transparency, accessibility, and receptibility, all which make her
the ideal candidate to represent El Monte’s constituents. Amy is an asset to her
community, and I am confident that her leadership and strong commitment to public
health, housing, and sustainability will address challenges from the pandemic and
ensure a bright and equitable future for generations to come. Please appoint Amy J.
Wong for El Monte City Council.

Anthony Contrado – My name is Anthony Contrado, I live in El Monte, and am a full-
time student at UCLA. I support Amy J. Wong for city council. As someone who has
lived in El Monte for the past six years, I cannot claim to know the true values of
being an El Montean. However, what I can say is that when I see Amy working with
our community, I see those values. I see someone who cares about their community
and will strive to make their community be the best it can be. I have had the
pleasure of knowing Amy for these last four years and I believe having her on
council would be putting El Monte in caring hands. I first met Amy when I was
volunteering for Active SGV, formerly known as Bike SGV. As someone fairly new to
El Monte, Amy had made me feel welcomed. She valued everyone’s thoughts
equally, whether it was a volunteer or an employee. Amy is a strong woman who
cares for everyone. Every event I have seen her at, she is always making sure the
attendees are having their needs met. She will go above and beyond what is
required of her to listen to everyone so they know they have been heard and to
show that their voices matter. Amy has the experience to lead, she has the heart to
listen and she has the willpower to put thoughts into action. I believe Amy to be the
best choice for City Council. Please appoint Amy J. Wong to the El Monte City
Council. Thank you for your time.

Irma Bustamante – My name is Irma Bustamante, I live in El Monte, and work as a
Health Clerk at the Covina Valley Unified School District. I support Amy J. Wong for
City Council. I met Amy when I signed up to volunteer for Active SGV four years ago
in March 2016. I remember my first impression of Amy was that she was very
approachable and easy to talk to, super kind, and was dedicated to improving the
lives of others through her work. Through these past four years, I’ve become good
friends with Amy, and I can say with full confidence that she truly cares about the
needs of people being met. I’ve never met someone so passionate about public
health and environmental justice. Whenever I talk to Amy, she always expresses so
much motivation in envisioning a healthier and happier El Monte because she
believes that the community deserves equity in overall living, health, housing, and
preventing the growth in numbers from COVID-19. As a disabled person, this is
incredibly significant to me in that I rarely hear about inclusiveness for the disabled
community. Disabled people are vulnerable to conditions like poor air quality, and
these kinds of problems need to be addressed and followed through with a plan.
This has always been something on Amy’s vision board, and she’s always someone
to follow through with her ideas and proposals. I admire Amy for her empathy, sense
of community, and for bringing people together, collectively, in order to improve our
overall well-being. I trust Amy to lead El Monte in the right direction to providing the
community with equitable resources to help us strive for healthier lives. Please
appoint Amy J. Wong to the El Monte City Council. Thank you.

Efren Moreno Jr. – My name is Efren Moreno Jr. and I am a former Alhambra City
Council member and a co-founder of BikeSGV. I highly encourage you to appoint
my J. Wong to the El Monte City Council. She is the best choice to represent the

  9
   City Council Special Meeting Minutes of January 26, 2021

residents and businesses of the city. I first met Amy in 2015 as a volunteer for
BikeSGV, now ActiveSGV, where her work was essential to the growth of the
organization and the service we provide to the San Gabriel Valley community. Amy
Wong has the knowledge and experience to be an advocate for healthy, sustainable
living for the residents of El Monte, through her work and volunteering for over six
years with various public health and environmental justice organizations in El Monte
and the San Gabriel Valley. She is a first-generation Asian-American born and
raised in El Monte. She went off to UC Berkeley and earned her degree and
returned to her hometown to serve the community. She has served for three years
on the El Monte Planning Commission, where difficult and complex issues are
discussed and resolved. Her character,  knowledge, and community experience
make her the best choice for an appointment to the El Monte City Council. Thank
